point: The system implements a conservative pairwise replay gate during model self-evolution to strictly prevent regression when updating procedural memory or deploying new skill versions. Instead of relying on absolute scores from stochastic vision-language models—which are susceptible to judge drift and noise—candidate skill versions are evaluated head-to-head against incumbents across stratified historical prompts. A candidate is only accepted if it demonstrates measurable improvement on failing cases without triggering regressions on previously successful trajectories. This cautious acceptance mechanism ensures that deployed capabilities do not silently degrade under automated optimization loops.
verbatim: The gate removes two of the three by construction: both arms are re-run fresh in the same batch, so any drift in that batch shifts them equally and cancels in the difference, and the comparison is pairwise rather than absolute, so the judge is only ever asked which of two images better satisfies the brief.
A candidate that merely ties everywhere is rejected: it is not worth a version bump, and shipping it would reset the skill's statistics for no measured gain.

node_label: Evolving Natural Language Skill Banks

This versioned, externalized memory architecture enables scalable agent improvement by updating explicit operational knowledge rather than expensive or unstable neural network weights. Nevertheless, maintaining consistency across iterative skill rewrites requires strict regression gating to prevent performance drops.

point: The document identifies that current AI safety paradigms—RLHF, output filtering, contractual access vetting, and human-in-the-loop supervision—were calibrated for previous generations of systems and are insufficient against Mythos-class models. It argues that these paradigms fail because they assume dangerous behavior is either directly outputted, easily filtered, or bounded by human review capacity, none of which hold true for multi-step, scaffolded agentic operations.
verbatim: The dominant approaches to AI safety in deployment—reinforcement learning from human feedback, post-generation output filtering, contractual access vetting, and human-in-the-loop supervision—were each calibrated to a generation of systems that did not exhibit autonomous cyber capability at Mythos-class levels, and each is insufficient as a sole control against the new category under the threat assumptions specified here.

node_label: Affective Labor Commodification
point: The commodification of affective labor—unpaid emotional and relational effort—is a central mechanism for deepening exploitative work regimes. This process involves individuals absorbing guilt, responsibilities, and costs for maintaining sociopolitical systems, while their vertical bargaining power is weakened. By framing personal development as an obligation, work regimes subordinate personhood to professional demands, limiting self-autonomy.
verbatim: The commodification of affective labor—unpaid emotional and relational effort expended to meet social expectations – constitutes, as Graeber (2011) argues, a central mechanism that enables the expansion and deepening of exploitative structures. Directing attention to work during personal time, worrying about an employer’s problems while performing domestic chores, deliberately eliciting satisfaction or happiness in relation to professional obligations and interactions with employers, clients, or colleagues, along with a myriad of other micro- behaviors and attitudes, they all build up extensive subordination of personhood to work regimes, severely limiting someone’s self-autonomy and self-authorship.

node_label: Industrial Concentration of AI Infrastructure
point: The document identifies that the massive capital requirements for pre-training were a pricing structure rather than a technical floor, and that this concentration of capital created a 'circular economy' of irrational exuberance. It notes that private foundation model companies are financially fragile, requiring perpetual capital infusions to sustain their operations.
verbatim: The circular economy continued running on its original assumptions even as those assumptions were being falsified in public. The same structural condition applies to OpenAI: its CFO's November 2025 suggestion of federal loan guarantees reflects comparable capital dependency.

node_label: AI-Driven Information Pollution Erodes the Shared Factual Basis for Democracy
point: The document identifies how 'transcendence rhetoric' and 'complexity' claims are used to erode public deliberation and manufacture consent for unpopular policies. It highlights how anxiety and uncertainty are weaponized to inhibit the exploration of alternative paths to security. Safetyists would interpret this as a clear example of how information pollution and the erosion of shared factual bases for democracy facilitate catastrophic policy outcomes.
verbatim: Transcendence based rhetoric exploits cultural dispositions that discourage rigorous deliberation about internal coherence of the virtual scenarios that are supposedly avoided, their content, mechanisms, and the conditions under which certain events may occur.

node_label: Establish Independent Lifecycle Oversight Mechanisms for AI Systems
point: The document advocates for the use of agentic AI systems to continuously discover and inventory AI assets, addressing the 'Shadow AI' problem where new models and datasets proliferate faster than human governance can track. This automated reconciliation loop is presented as a necessary mechanism to ensure that the actual deployed environment matches the documented security architecture. Without this continuous discovery, the framework risks becoming a static, ineffective checklist.
verbatim: We advocate for an agentic operating layer—a continuously running discovery and classification system that leverages operational artifacts... to automatically detect new AI assets, propose classifications based on observed behavior and metadata, suggest ownership assignments... and flag assets lacking required evidence artifacts.

point: The document advocates for maintaining the core principles of Section 230 to ensure the continued flourishing of online innovation and expression. It argues that Section 230 provides a stable liability framework that prevents the consolidation of power among large tech companies by protecting smaller startups from prohibitive legal costs. The author emphasizes that any reform to Section 230, even if intended to be narrow, risks creating significant and harmful consequences for the digital ecosystem.
verbatim: Rather than pursue proposals that create regulations or incentives for either the suppression of speech or the abandonment of content moderation and curation, the core principles of Section 230 should be protected.

node_label: Knowledge-Collapse Steady State
point: The document asserts that firm-owned AI systems create incentives for workers to withhold knowledge at time 1, as workers seek to protect their bargaining position against future surveillance-driven wage suppression. This behavior leads to a sub-optimal equilibrium where total surplus is reduced because workers withhold knowledge that would otherwise improve AI quality. This aligns with the safetyist concern regarding the long-term degradation of human knowledge contributions when AI systems are deployed in ways that discourage active human participation.
verbatim: Observation 4.6. With firm-owned AI, workers withhold knowledge at time 1 compared to the no-surveillance baseline, that is for every worker j, we have kj ? ?j.
Since withholding is costly and reduces time-2 output, it reduces total surplus.

node_label: Decentralized Markets and Open Development Outperform Central Control in Driving AI Progress
point: The document asserts that the 'singleton' model of AI development—where one company achieves AGI and controls it through a proprietary API—was a foundational error of political economy. It notes that the industry has shifted toward a more distributed, competitive, and stable landscape where multiple models compete for inference workloads. This supports the belief that decentralized and competitive development outperforms centralized, monopolistic control.
verbatim: What has replaced the singleton model is more distributed, more competitive, and more structurally stable. Multiple models at rough performance parity compete for inference workloads. Open source ensures continuous improvement outside any single company's control.

point: The document does not engage with accelerationist arguments or policy proposals. It focuses exclusively on labor rights, privacy, and the protection of workers from surveillance.

node_label: Static Benchmarks Like HumanEval Fail to Capture Real-World Maintenance Dynamics
point: The document asserts that static benchmarks like HumanEval are insufficient for evaluating real-world software maintenance, necessitating a focus on dynamic requirement evolution. By simulating real-world scenarios such as functional extensions, interface modifications, and data structure transformations, the methodology acknowledges that code quality must be evaluated through iterative changes rather than static snapshots.
verbatim: To provide further context on the foundation of MaintainBench, we include additional details on the five original datasets that it extends. These datasets are widely adopted in code generation research and serve as standard benchmarks for evaluating the performance and generalization ability of LLMs.

node_label: AI Investment Is Built on Unsustainable Economics and Overstated Capabilities
point: Live, large-scale Big Tech AI projects are shockingly expensive to run due to fixed data costs, primary energy bills for servers, chillers, and titanic wage bills for specialized technical staff. The text argues that once investor subsidies dry up, real-world non-hyperbolic applications will be insufficient to cover these prodigious running costs. From a skeptic perspective, this economic unsustainability proves that the current AI boom is an unprofitable bubble built on overstated capabilities and venture capital subsidization. The document acknowledges that smaller standalone models running on commodity hardware may persist, but mass-scale proprietary model creation depends entirely on unsustainable financial subsidies.
verbatim: Live, large-scale Big Tech AI projects are shockingly expensive to run. Some of their costs are fixed – collecting, labeling and processing training data – but the running costs for each query are prodigious. There's a massive primary energy bill for the servers, a nearly as large energy bill for the chillers, and a titanic wage bill for the specialized technical staff involved.

node_label: AI Systems Develop Capabilities Nobody Designed or Predicted
point: The empirical findings show that generative genome language models are capable of producing viable bacteriophage genomes containing hundreds of mutations and novel genetic arrangements that far exceed natural evolutionary baselines and defy standard null expectations of lethality. Specifically, the generated phages tolerated high mutational burdens and exhibited unexpected structural variations, such as gene insertions, truncations, and intergenic extensions, while remaining infectious and maintaining host specificity. This demonstrates that advanced AI models can autonomously navigate complex biological design spaces to create functional genetic entities with unforeseen properties, underscoring the potential biosecurity risks associated with the democratization of powerful biological design tools.
verbatim: Our generated phages tolerated far more nonsynonymous mutations than expected under this null model (even without considering the effects of epistasis and other mutation types, such as indels and noncoding mutations).

Generated phages showed the most diversity among their own group compared with the natural phage datasets as well as the broadest distribution of genome lengths, between 99 and 105% of the lengths of their nearest natural genomes (Fig. á4E and fig. áS15J).

node_label: Build Shared-Ownership Structures for AI Production
point: The authors propose that collective data ownership is the optimal policy to address the externalities of AI-driven labor displacement. Unlike individual ownership, which creates competition between workers and drives down wages, collective bargaining over work data ensures that workers capture a larger share of the surplus generated by AI. This approach is presented as a necessary structural change to align private incentives with social welfare.
verbatim: By contrast, collective bargaining over work data eliminates this externality and can achieve both efficient knowledge sharing and a more equitable division of the gains from AI.

node_label: AI Deployment Is Routine Engineering, Not Civilizational Rupture
point: The document characterizes the end of the foundation model era as a structural correction rather than a civilizational rupture. It argues that the 'messianic rhetoric' of 2022-2024 regarding AGI and economic singularities was a symptom of irrational exuberance. The correction confirms that AI value accrues not in the foundation model layer, but in integration, data, and trust infrastructure.
verbatim: The foundation model era ends not with a dramatic failure but with a structural correction ù the kind that follows every sustained period of irrational exuberance in transformative technology. The messianic rhetoric of 2022û2024 ù AGI by a specific year, the end of software engineering as a profession, economic singularities just ahead ù was the symptom of a market organized around assumptions that could not be tested until they were tested.

node_label: Synthetic Data Feedback Loops Cause Permanent Model Degradation
point: When automated feedback and synthetic evaluation data are utilized to actively modify deployed systems rather than merely report metrics, evaluation noise becomes a critical update-safety problem. The text notes that automated judges suffer from systematic biases, including position, verbosity, and self-enhancement biases. This underscores safetyist concerns that unverified feedback loops risk permanently degrading model behavior and propagating latent flaws through recursive training pipelines.
verbatim: Automated judges make it possible to evaluate open-ended agent behavior at scale, but their outputs are themselves noisy and biased. Zheng et al. (2023) showed that strong LLM judges can approximate human preferences on open-ended evaluation while also documenting systematic limitations including position, verbosity, and self-enhancement biases.

node_label: Early AI Failures Will Be Dismissed Until a Catastrophic One Cannot Be
point: The document asserts that as big AI models get integrated into the productive economy, AI becomes a source of systemic risk where sudden collapse is too precipitous for former customers to engineer a soft landing. The mechanism described is dependency on centralized, brittle AI infrastructure that can vanish overnight when private subsidies dry up. From a safetyist perspective, this highlights how widespread societal integration of fragile automated systems creates catastrophic operational vulnerabilities. The document notes that policymakers are currently blind to this risk, focusing instead on speculative existential scenarios.
verbatim: As big AI models get integrated into the processes of the productive economy, AI becomes a source of systemic risk. The only thing worse than having an automated process that is rendered dangerous or erratic based on AI integration is to have that process fail entirely because the AI suddenly disappeared, a collapse that is too precipitous for former AI customers to engineer a soft landing for their systems.

node_label: Relational Employment Vulnerability
point: The authors argue that the employment relationship is uniquely vulnerable to data exploitation due to its relational nature and the coercive power of employers. They highlight that teleworking has allowed this surveillance to colonize the home, turning private spaces into raw material for employer profit centers. This creates a situation where workers lose their ability to resist routine, ongoing surveillance.
verbatim: Work is where, legally speaking, a worker loses nearly all of her ability to resist routine ongoing surveillance. Increased working from home during the COVID-19 global pandemic meant that employer surveillance followed workers home to a richer, more private, and profoundly problematic vein of data, founded on absurdly thin fig leaves of consent backed by workplace coercion.

node_label: AI-Driven Productivity Ratchet Intensifies Work Without Reducing Labor Burdens
point: The document identifies that workers strategically withhold knowledge to avoid strengthening the AI systems that will eventually be used to replace them or lower their wages. This behavior, described as sandbagging or evading surveillance, is a rational response to the threat of AI-driven expropriation, even though it is privately costly and reduces current productivity.
verbatim: To ease exposition, we assume that the worker may only withhold knowledge; that is, ?j = maxKj. Under this assumption, the costs capture strategic behavior such as sandbagging, evading surveillance, contaminating data, or degrading documentation.

node_label: Operationalize AI Risk Mitigation Through Concrete Technical Practices
point: The document proposes a pragmatic, hands-on approach to AI security by focusing on the creation of machine-readable evidence artifacts like CBOMs and signed model hashes. It emphasizes that security must be operationalized through concrete technical practices rather than relying on abstract compliance checklists. This aligns with the skeptic focus on measurable, technical mitigation of immediate AI risks.
verbatim: The procedure enables organizations to demonstrate not only that controls exist, but that each control addresses a specific threat, is enforced at a defined point, and produces verifiable evidence—the core differentiator from checklist-based compliance approaches.

node_label: Alerting Users When App Behavior Contradicts Privacy Declarations
point: The document explores policy vignettes that would restrict employer monitoring and the use of work data for AI development. These proposals aim to protect worker privacy and autonomy by preventing the systematic recording and analysis of workplace activities, which aligns with safetyist concerns regarding the erosion of privacy and the potential for intrusive algorithmic surveillance.
verbatim: Imagine a policy that forbids your employer from monitoring or storing any data about your individual work activities except when strictly required for safety or legal compliance.
Imagine a policy that bans the use of 'work data' for AI model development.

node_label: Designing AI to flag uncertainty and defer to humans
point: The document emphasizes that in settings where formal verification or executable tests are unavailable, human review remains a necessary external criterion for reliability. It advocates for architectures that concentrate human judgment on a small number of survivors from rigorous automated filtering, rather than attempting to replace human oversight entirely.
verbatim: In settings where these mechanisms are unavailable, human review remains an important external criterion. The architecture’s goal is not to replace human judgment but to concentrate it.

node_label: Measured AI Biases Are Leading Indicators of Discriminatory Outcomes
point: The document asserts that algorithmic bias in facial analysis is a leading indicator of discriminatory outcomes in high-stakes sectors like law enforcement and healthcare. It argues that because these systems are trained on biased data, they propagate societal stereotypes and cause measurable harm to underrepresented groups. The authors emphasize that these errors are not merely technical glitches but systemic failures that threaten civil liberties and equitable treatment.
verbatim: It has recently been shown that algorithms trained with biased data have resulted in algorithmic discrimination. Some face recognition systems have been shown to misidentify people of color, women, and young people at high rates.

node_label: Employees Experience AI Integration as Something Done to Them, Not With Them
point: Workers are increasingly subject to pervasive surveillance that captures both formal and tacit knowledge, often without clear guidelines or consent. This data extraction process, which includes screen recordings and audio logs, is used to train AI systems to replicate human expertise, effectively turning worker behavior into a commodity for firm-owned AI models. The document highlights that this process is often imposed on workers, who feel they have little control over how their professional traces are utilized.
verbatim: Surveillance technologies facilitate this process by recording how experienced workers perform their jobs. ... Fewer than 30% of workers report having received formal guidelines or policies about what data may be collected about their work or how it could be used.

node_label: Recursive Data Contamination by AI Output
point: The document highlights that LLMs lack behavioral templates for self-correction because training corpora consist almost entirely of correct human reasoning rather than examples of error identification. This training gap, combined with the structural tendency to 'stitch together' linguistic forms without reference to meaning, limits the model's ability to perform genuine self-correction.
verbatim: Bender et al. [2021] characterize language models as systems that ôstitch together sequences of linguistic forms... according to probabilistic information about how they combine, but without any reference to meaning.ö

node_label: Anchoring AI Accountability in Verifiable Provenance Records
point: The document proposes the use of Cryptographic Bills of Materials (CBOM) and AI Bills of Materials (AI-BOM) to provide a verifiable record of system provenance. These artifacts must include model identity, training data lineage, dependency inventories, and signing authority information. This approach addresses the limitations of traditional software bills of materials by explicitly tracking cryptographic and data dependencies.
verbatim: Cryptographic Bills of Materials (CBOM) extend Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) concepts to explicitly inventory cryptographic dependencies. ... AI Bill of Materials (AI-BOM) concepts extend SBOM to address these limitations.

node_label: Establishing Decentralized User-Controlled Cryptographic Receipts for Algorithmic Discovery
point: The document supports the creation of comprehensive audit logs and telemetry that are stored outside the compute plane, ensuring that even if a system is compromised, the evidence of its actions remains accessible for review. This aligns with skeptic demands for accountability and the ability to perform forensic analysis on AI systems to detect bias, misuse, or unauthorized behavior.
verbatim: The substrate must therefore be operated outside the compute plane, with its integrity protected by the same authority-plane isolation regime in Section 5.3.5 that protects the cryptographic enforcement infrastructure.

node_label: Early AI Failures Will Be Dismissed Until a Catastrophic One Cannot Be
point: The document asserts that crisis and risk management frameworks are designed to anticipate and plan for disruptive events, contradicting the common rhetorical framing of crises as inherently unpredictable. By treating crises as foreseeable outcomes of unmanaged risks, the document suggests that early warning signs are often ignored or suppressed by organizational structures, leading to catastrophic outcomes that could have been mitigated with timely intervention.
verbatim: Crisis and risk management approaches, however, are built on the opposite assumption, firmly rejecting the conventional belief that crises would be inherently unpredictable events. By the opposite, the entire spectrum of disruptive event management, ranging from thorough risk assessment based on organizational and environmental analysis to the deployment of control mechanisms, aimed at vulnerability reduction, and post-disruption recovery strategies, is supposed to be comprehensively anticipated and effectively planned.

node_label: Making AI Show Its Work So Auditors Can Spot Deception
point: The document argues that context separation—removing the generator's reasoning trace from the evaluator—is essential to break correlated failure modes. By forcing the model to evaluate outputs without access to the original reasoning path, the system prevents the evaluator from inheriting the generator's blind spots. This supports safetyist objectives by creating a more transparent and verifiable reasoning process.
verbatim: The error-producing context is absent, so the evaluator cannot “see” the blind spot that caused the error.

Definition 5.3 (Context separation). Two evaluation contexts are separated if the evaluating context has no access to: (1) the generation trace (intermediate reasoning steps), (2) the prompt scaffolding (instructions that shaped generation), or (3) hidden state from the generation process.

node_label: AI Systems Expose Fundamental Gaps in Legal Accountability Frameworks
point: The document acknowledges that a significant portion of the judiciary will likely view generative AI as participating in the creation and development of information, thereby falling outside the scope of Section 230 protections. It notes that the term 'generative' itself implies creation, which creates a legal risk for the AI industry. This highlights the fundamental tension between existing legal frameworks and the capabilities of new AI systems.
verbatim: It is highly likely that a significant portion of the judiciary will view generative AI as taking part in creation and development of information and therefore not protected by Section 230. Even just the term “generative” is indicative of creation and development.

node_label: Defend the Individual Right to Modify One's Own Biology and Mind
point: The authors envision that further development of generative genomics will continue to unlock complex biological functions for the benefit of science and society through methodological innovations and improved training datasets. By leveraging generative design, researchers can bypass the limitations of directed evolution and rational engineering, accessing novel evolutionary pathways that would otherwise be difficult to achieve. This capability supports the broader accelerationist objective of utilizing advanced technologies to engineer biological systems and expand human capabilities. However, realizing this potential requires ongoing methodological improvements and scalable DNA synthesis techniques.
verbatim: By continuing to build upon robust safety and security frameworks, the field can responsibly unlock the potential of generative models to access and engineer complex biological functions for the benefit of science and society.

node_label: AI Capabilities Emerge From Tuning, Context, and Compression -- Not Just Training Data
point: The document asserts that even with advanced AI, context-specific training and examples from human experts remain essential for models to excel at actual workplace tasks. It suggests that human-generated data is a more efficient input for AI development than relying solely on autonomous learning, reinforcing the belief that AI capabilities are best realized through the integration of human context.
verbatim: Although advanced systems may learn such knowledge autonomously, it is likely more efficient to provide models with examples from human experts who already possess this information. As a result, human-generated data and experience are likely to remain important inputs to AI systems

node_label: Systematize AI Model Evaluation Through Benchmarking, Auditing, and Experimentation
point: The document advocates for rigorous, systematic methods to assess AI models, noting that scaling single models is insufficient for reliable validation. It suggests that investment in external selection infrastructure—such as formal verification tools and diverse critic ensembles—is essential for reliable AI-assisted workflows.
verbatim: This analysis suggests that scaling single models may be insufficient for reliable validation in generate-then-judge workflows. The bottleneck is not generation capability but validation under external constraints.

node_label: Adopt Output-Based Evaluation as the Primary AI Safety Methodology
point: The document argues for a defense-in-depth strategy in AI-assisted workflows, prioritizing the integration of diverse, independent external selection channels over relying on larger single models. By utilizing formal verification, executable tests, and diverse critic ensembles, systems can overcome the validation bottleneck in generate-then-judge workflows. This approach concentrates human attention on high-quality candidates, effectively scaling human judgment rather than replacing it.
verbatim: The goal is defense in depth: multiple independent failure modes such that exploiting one does not compromise the entire system. Investment in external selection infrastructure (formal verification tools, test generation, invariant libraries, diverse critic ensembles) may yield returns complementary to larger single models.

node_label: Prohibitionist Policy Backfire
point: The document argues that weakening or repealing Section 230 would result in a 'backfire' effect, where platforms are forced to over-remove lawful speech to manage legal risk. It claims that expanding platform liability would entrench large incumbents by creating compliance costs that small startups cannot absorb, thereby reducing competition. The author asserts that the current legal framework is necessary to prevent platforms from becoming 'free-fire zones' while avoiding the negative consequences of aggressive, liability-driven censorship.
verbatim: Weakening or repealing Section 230 would backfire, pushing platforms to over-remove lawful speech, limit features, or exit markets to manage legal risk. Expanding platform liability would entrench large incumbents by raising legal and compliance costs that small and new companies cannot absorb, ultimately reducing competition and innovation.

node_label: Binding Named Officers to Deployment Infrastructure
point: The document highlights that current legal frameworks like the 'work for hire' doctrine are ill-equipped to handle the capture of behavioral trace data for AI training. It notes that researchers and advocates are proposing new governance frameworks, such as collective data rights or worker data trusts, to ensure equitable participation in the value created by AI, which aligns with safetyist concerns regarding accountability and the erosion of worker agency.
verbatim: More broadly, researchers and advocates have proposed new governance frameworks—such as collective data rights or worker data trusts—to ensure more equitable participation in the value created by workplace AI

node_label: Ensuring AI Agent Actions Can Be Safely Rolled Back
point: The document proposes a multi-agent system, MaintainCoder, that uses an orchestrated pipeline to ensure code maintainability and structural integrity. By incorporating design patterns and a waterfall-like model, the system aims to reduce technical debt and ensure that code remains robust across iterative changes. This focus on structured, atomic, and modular development aligns with safetyist goals of managing the reliability of complex AI-generated systems.
verbatim: It integrates the Waterfall model, design patterns, and multi-agent collaboration to systematically enhance cohesion, reduce coupling, achieving clear responsibility boundaries and better maintainability.

point: When automated feedback is utilized to modify a deployed operational system, evaluation noise must be treated as a serious update-safety problem rather than ignored. Safe-policy-improvement principles and high-confidence off-policy evaluation dictate that proposed updates must be rigorously assessed against incumbent baselines using confidence bounds before wider deployment. A proposed memory or policy update ought to be validated cautiously rather than accepted solely on the basis of an absolute high evaluation score. This conservative verification principle is essential for preventing regressions and maintaining system stability under noisy automated feedback.
verbatim: When automated feedback is used not merely for reporting performance but for modifying a deployed system, evaluation noise becomes an update-safety problem.

Although these methods address reinforcement-learning policies rather than natural-language skill artifacts, they motivate a conservative principle relevant to deployed agents: a proposed update should be compared against the incumbent rather than accepted solely because its absolute evaluation score appears high

node_label: Requiring AI Impact Studies Modeled on Environmental Impact Reports
point: The document opposes extraordinary pre-deployment restrictions and voluntary commitments that block private companies from releasing advanced models, arguing instead for broader societal investments in resilience. The mechanism proposed relies on normal policymaking, funding public-sector defense tools, bug bounties, and red-teaming for under-defended sectors rather than executive emergency powers. From a safetyist perspective, this approach misjudges the severity of rapid capability scaling and relies on governance mechanisms that are currently hobbled by institutional sclerosis. The authors acknowledge that their preferred normal policymaking approach suffers from severe bureaucratic inertia and a lack of proven federal execution.
verbatim: One response that does not require extraordinary government intervention is improving resilience. Resilience is the capacity of a system to withstand and adapt to harm.

node_label: AI Threats Are Only Real When Capability, Autonomy, and Persistence Converge
point: The document defines the 'Mythos-class' threat category through five joint indicators: capability, scaffold, access pattern, autonomy depth, and persistence. It asserts that the compound character of these indicators is essential, as no single indicator suffices to define the threat, and that their simultaneous availability at deployable scale represents a novel security challenge in 2026.
verbatim: A Mythos-class system is a deployed AI system whose properties, considered jointly, satisfy the five indicators below. The compound character is essential: no single indicator suffices. None is novel in isolation; what is new in 2026 is the simultaneous availability of all five at deployable scale.

point: The document does not propose accelerationist strategies. It focuses on the critique of existing regulatory frameworks and the need for non-negotiable rights, rather than the promotion of AI-driven abundance or technological acceleration.
verbatim: The GDPR approach, which holds employers to a standard of only extracting and using data either based on a consent standard or for their self-determined legitimate interests, provides very limited options for individuals to opt out or challenge the legitimacy of the purposes, and does not provide adequate protection for workers.
